title: Unified devbox auth patterns: OS secret stores, token-exchange, streaming reauth and rotation samples for Python/TS/Go
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
Provide a single, pragmatic reference implementation and guidance for developer machines (devbox), CI, and light-weight production agents that need to use Redwood SDKs in Python, TypeScript, and Go. The goal is to reduce insecure copy-paste of API keys and one-off SSO hacks by: 1) integrating with OS secret stores (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Linux Secret Service), 2) documenting a secure local token-exchange flow for SSO (OIDC code exchange -> short-lived SDK token), 3) demonstrating safe key rotation patterns and leakage mitigation, and 4) improving SDK streaming re-auth ergonomics so live streams can seamlessly refresh tokens without dropping user-facing streams.

Why this now:
- Customers (enterprise and startups) repeatedly ask for secure local auth patterns and CI best practices.
- We see recurring support tickets where leaked long-lived API keys were found in dotfiles and CI logs.
- Streaming reauth issues: customers report dropped streaming connections on token rotations and unusual retry spikes.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
- Provide three reference helpers (Python/TS/Go) that: a) read credentials from OS secret store, b) fallback to ephemeral SSO token exchange, and c) perform automatic rotation with safe caching and jittered refresh.
- Add a small 'devbox auth CLI' recipe (npm / pip / go install example) that sets up secure storage and performs OIDC exchange with recommended scopes and lifetime.
- Update SDKs with a minimal TokenProvider interface and examples for streaming reauth hook to resume without full reconnect where supported.
- Documentation: clear migration guide, checklist for CI/CD, and an audit checklist to detect leaks.

Design notes and constraints:
- Introduce a TokenProvider abstraction (language-specific): get_token(), refresh_if_needed(), revoke() - implemented as a pluggable strategy for OSStoreProvider, EnvVarProvider (deprecated for devboxes), and SSOExchangeProvider. Do not change existing public high-level SDK API shapes; expose opt-in token_provider argument to client factory functions.
- OS store implementations must use native libraries or well-maintained bindings (keyring for Python, keytar for Node, go-keyring). Keep code paths small and explicit to ease security review.
- Token lifetimes: prefer short-lived SDK tokens (<= 1 hour). When exchanging from SSO, use audience-restricted tokens. Provide guidance and code to store refresh token encrypted in OS store, not in plaintext files.
- Streaming reauth: add a lightweight reauth callback that returns a valid Authorization header; the runtime will attempt in-place token swap for open streaming channels and only fall back to reconnect when server rejects with an unrecoverable code. Include exponential backoff + jitter for auth-related retries distinct from network retries.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Reference implementations for Python, TypeScript, and Go live in the repo under /sdk/examples/devbox-auth and include README with setup steps.
- CI recipe validated: a GitHub Actions example that uses OIDC runner_token exchange and stores ephemeral token in GitHub Actions secrets for a single job.
- SDKs accept a token_provider parameter and document migration steps; no breaking changes to default client constructors.
- Streaming reauth hook implemented in at least two SDKs (Python + TS) with integration tests that simulate rotation and validate <5s user-perceived interruption in ideal network conditions.
- Security review completed and checklist items resolved (keystore libs vetted, no logging of secrets, tests for accidental env leak scanning).

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) 1 week: Spec PR with TokenProvider interface, code examples sketch, and security checklist.
2) 2 weeks: Implement OS store helpers for Python (keyring) and Node (keytar), plus Go binding. Add unit tests.
3) 1 week: Add SSO exchange helper and devbox CLI recipe.
4) 1 week: Streaming reauth hook implementation and integration tests (Python + TS).
5) 1 week: Docs, migration guide, and security review.

Migration notes for customers:
- Default behavior unchanged: existing API_KEY env var usage still works, but we will add warnings in README encouraging OS key store usage for long-term devboxes.
- For enterprises using SSO, the recommended flow is: OIDC -> short-lived refresh token stored in OS store -> SDK token exchange for per-session tokens.

Risk and mitigations:
- Risk: OS keyring dependencies may be brittle across Linux distros. Mitigation: add fallbacks and clear troubleshooting docs; include a shim that can fallback to an encrypted file using the system's KMS in extreme cases.
- Risk: Streaming reauth complexity could introduce subtle race conditions. Mitigation: keep API surface minimal, add thorough integration tests, roll out as opt-in flag before defaulting.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for token provider implementations and edge cases (expired tokens, concurrent refresh).
- Integration test that spins up a local auth-mock and streaming mock to verify token swaps without full reconnect.
- Fuzz test for credential serialization and keyring errors.

Documentation deliverables:
- /docs/sdk/devbox-auth.md with step-by-step guides for macOS/Windows/Linux.
- Code snippets for Python/TS/Go to copy into README of sample app.
- Migration checklist for support and onboarding.

Rollout and telemetry:
- Rollout initially behind a feature flag opt-in in SDK releases; gather telemetry (auth failure rates, reauth attempts, streaming reconnects) via existing diagnostics with opt-in telemetry.

Open questions for design review:
- What is the canonical minimum token lifetime we should recommend for SDK tokens? (30m vs 1h)
- Should we provide an official devbox CLI distribution or just recipes?
- Which exact auth error codes should trigger in-place streaming reauth vs full reconnect?

References and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SDK/Devbox+Auth+Patterns (draft)
- Example PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4521 (TokenProvider sketch)
- Security checklist doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/security/sdk-key-handling-checklist.pdf
acceptance_criteria: Python/TS/Go reference examples added under sdk/examples/devbox-auth with setup READMEs
TokenProvider abstraction implemented and documented in SDKs as opt-in parameter
Streaming reauth hook added to Python and TypeScript SDKs with integration tests
Security review completed and third-party keyring libraries approved
CI example (GitHub Actions) demonstrating ephemeral job-scoped tokens
